summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free browser game for children aged 7 to 12. The player keeps a one-person outpost at the lunar south pole running for 32 game days while the crew is away. Every day brings real trade-offs: 10 kW of sunlight must be shared between life support, food lights, science and storm watch, while oxygen, water and food must last. Every storm in the game copies a real solar flare recorded in NASA's DONKI space weather database, and the player must read the forecast and reach the radiation shelter in time. Short sourced info cards turn each mechanic into a real science fact. It runs in any desktop browser with no installation, and a Judge mode lets reviewers jump to any day or event.
details:
WHAT IT DOES:
The player runs a lunar south-pole outpost for 32 game days (each day lasts 4 real minutes). They eat, drink, water radishes, share 10 kW of solar power between four systems (life support, food lights, science, storm watch), clean panels dimmed by lander dust, swap power packs, collect cargo, go on missions (rock and soil, an ice-dig mini-game, and a final rare stone), process samples at the lab, read the storm forecast, and shelter from solar storms. The ending shows research %, 1 to 5 stars, and 'What you learned'.

TRY IT IN 2 MINUTES:
Open the game link, click Judge mode, choose the preset 'Storm during a mission', collect the sample, and walk to the shelter before the countdown ends. For the full run, click Start Game. Controls: arrows or WASD, E to interact, Esc for the menu.

KEY FEATURES:
8 storms copied from real NASA DONKI flares, labelled on screen with class and date; a Space Weather Log listing them; crater-rim shadow days with no solar power; long polar shadows that turn with the clock; health, blackout and failed missions; a guided tutorial and daily checklist for young players; sourced info cards and a Fact log; autosave, manual save and Retry day; a Judge mode with presets and a clean Video mode.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT:
Children practise planning, cause and effect, and risk, the same choices a real crew makes, while learning sourced facts about the Moon, the Sun and life support. It is free, runs in a browser with no installation or account, and a game day takes about 4 minutes, so it fits a classroom lesson.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE:
Every danger is tied to a real, dated observation. Each storm copies a real solar flare from NASA's DONKI database and names it on screen, and the finale is the X28 flare of 2003, the brightest X-ray flare ever measured. The south-pole sky is modelled as it really is: the Sun circles low on the horizon, long shadows turn with the clock, and crater-rim shadow days cut solar power, based on NASA's polar power studies.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED:
The age range 7 to 12 (icons before numbers, short cards, a guided tutorial, kind failure screens with Retry day); scientific honesty (every simplification is labelled, for example radishes grow about 4x faster than on the ISS); a small set of resources so the trade-offs stay clear (power, life support, food); access (browser, no install, keyboard only, works offline once loaded); and reviewers with little time (Judge mode).

TOOLS:
Godot Engine 4.7.2 (GDScript) exported to WebAssembly; Python 3.11 (DONKI download, asset preparation, sound generation); Pixel Lab (AI-generated pixel art); Claude Code (AI-assisted coding); Git. No special hardware.

EVIDENCE:
Automated tests run after every change. sim_check plays all 32 days with a scripted careful player and matches the design table (meals exactly, water within 0.1 L, research exactly); other tests cover endings and storm timing, every Judge button, save and load, oxygen and blackout, collisions, text overflow and audio. Play-tested in the browser by both team members and by independent AI play-testers.

WORKS NOW:
The full 32-day run with both endings, missions, storms, shadow days, saves, Judge mode, and sound.

LIMITS:
Desktop browser and keyboard only (no phones or tablets); English only; one save slot stored in the browser; time is compressed (labelled in the game); storms use archived flares, not live data; not yet tested with children.

FUTURE PLANS:
Arabic and touch controls, a teacher guide, a 'today's Sun' mode with live DONKI data, more crops and school testing.
